newsitem.title: UK: UK's ITC awards digital TV licence to S4C.
newsitem.headline: UK's ITC awards digital TV licence to S4C.

text.p: British broadcasting regulator, the Independent Television Commission (ITC), said on Monday it decided to award a licence to sole applicant S4C Digital Networks Ltd (SDN) to operate digital terrestrial television.
It said it intends to grant the licence within 12 weeks from today.

The ITC said in a statement that the award of the Multiplex Service Licence A was conditional on S4C's shareholding in SDN being no more than 50.1 percent and on the rest of the funding being from a shareholder or shareholders acceptable to the ITC.
SDN is already in discussions with interested parties.
S4C -- the digital subsidiary of Welsh Channel Four -- and Channel 5 have guaranteed capacity on Multiplex A, which is required to carry Gaelic programmes in Scotland.
The ITC awarded its B, C and D licences to British Digital Broadcasting -- a consortium comprising Carlton Communications Plc and Granada Group Plc -- on June 24.
